subject: Capacity & model-fit summary — NimbleBank next steps
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Laura Chen <laura.chen@nimblebank.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 22 Nov 2026 15:04:00 -0800
Subject: Capacity & model-fit summary — NimbleBank next steps

Hi Laura — great to meet earlier. Quick recap from our discovery and the recommended next steps. I kept this focused so we can share with your engineering and procurement teams.

Summary of your pain points
- End-user latency spikes: current p95 observed ~120-150ms for chat experiences; target is p95 <= 100ms across peak hours.
- Cost pressure during peak trading hours (daily morning spike); budget target is ~30% lower per-conversation cost versus current in-house serving.
- Data isolation requirement for PII-bearing queries (must run inside VPC with customer-managed KMS for keys).

Goals you stated
- Support 200 concurrent chat sessions with avg. 4 requests/sec/session at peak (roughly 800 req/s sustained, bursts to ~1.5k/s).
- Hit p95 latency <= 100ms for short-turn conversations (<=256 tokens).
- Keep initial rollout on dedicated capacity behind a VPC; optional private deployment for regulated flows.

Technical notes & model fit
- Model candidates: fine-tuned Mistral-family vs Llama-2-Chat derivatives. We recommend evaluating Mistral-Chat-7B-quant (int8) and a 13B variant if you need higher instruction alignment.
- Quantization/profile: int8 + KV cache enabled; will reduce GPU memory footprint and help hitting SLOs without larger instances.
- Batching: continuous batching with workload-aware batch windows (preferred) — expect 20–30% token-cost reduction at minimal p95 impact when tuned.

Proposed topology (short)
- Dedicated pool in us-west1 with autoscaling: baseline 4 A100s (for stateful KV caching + steady throughput) with burst capacity to 12 nodes during market open.
- Private control plane + VPC peering for PII flows. TLS + customer KMS for key management.
- Smart-routing policy: latency-first for customer-facing endpoints; cost-fallback to slightly cheaper quantized variant under pressure.

Requested next steps
1) Technical deep-dive with your infra/ML engineer + our solutions engineer (Marissa) — propose Tue 11/24 11:00 AM PT or Wed 11/25 2:00 PM PT.
2) I'll share a short topology sketch and preliminary perf estimates for the two model candidates (attached).
3) Procurement: if you can share procurement contact, we’ll prepare a draft commercial and SOW.

Attachments included: nimblebank-capacity-summary.pdf (this message), topology-sketch.png, performance-estimates.csv

Thanks again — Ben

--

- The p95 <= 100ms target applies to both web and API flows; mobile traffic is lower volume but higher sensitivity to tail latency.
- We have an existing KV cache layer in front of our stack (Redis) — curious how Redwood’s prefix/KV caching would integrate.
- Can you confirm which telemetry we can expect in Redwood Console for per-route token cost and per-device latency? We need that for our internal chargeback model.

Procurement (copied): please confirm what docs you need to start a commercial. Also need SOC2 Type II report and a short runbook for incident response for regulated flows.

I'll check availability for the proposed slots and circle back — Tuesday 11/24 11AM PT looks promising.

Laura / procurement — thanks. Quick answers and attachments attached below.

Answers to questions
- Telemetry: Redwood Console exposes per-route p50/p95/p99 latency, token-level cost breakdown, per-model throughput charts, and request traces (down to token timing). We can add a per-device latency dimension if you provide device identifiers in requests.
- KV cache integration: Redwood’s prefix/KV caching can sit in front of the model runtime or in a sidecar that reads your Redis instance for hot prefixes; for your setup we recommend sidecar read-through to avoid cache duplication.
- SOC2: posting a link to our SOC2 Type II bundle in the related links. We can provide a redacted report for procurement promptly.

Attached: topology-sketch.png (sketch of ded-pool + VPC peering), performance-estimates.csv (cost/latency projection for Mistral-7B-int8 vs Mistral-13B-int8).

Proposed next steps (updated)
- Technical deep-dive (Marissa + your infra lead): Tue 11/24 11:00 AM PT — if that works I’ll send a calendar invite with an agenda.
- Procurement: share a contact and we’ll seed a draft SOW + pricing sheet scoped to baseline + burst capacity.

If procurement needs an initial commercial stub now, we can run a one-page Term Sheet that covers: 12-month reserved pool option, monthly commit, and burst billing.

Regards,
Ben

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Date: Mon, 23 Nov 2026 08:45:00 -08:00
Subject: Internal: technical prep notes for NimbleBank deep-dive

Ben — internal notes I added after reviewing their load profile and our perf sims. Leaving this on-thread so you have the context. Please don’t forward this verbatim to the customer; I’ll prepare a cleaned agenda.

Key technical points
- With the workload (~800 req/s sustained, bursts to 1.5k/s) and p95 <=100ms target, A100s in a dedicated pool look right if we use int8+KV cache; recommend starting with 4 nodes (steady) + autoscale to 12 during bursts.
- Kernel & sequence-length tuning: use shorter sequence-optimized kernels for the 64–256 token range; larger sequences should be routed to a fallback model variant with higher memory.
- Network: place the pool in us-west1 with VPC peering; ensure cross-region fallback is available (us-east1) for DR.
- Observability: add a token-level cost alert and a p95 regression alert tied to a synthetic prompt set (we can ship a starter set).

Prep deliverables for the call
- A short topology sketch (attached by Ben)
- Perf tab that shows expected p95 vs concurrency for both candidate models
- A list of firewall rules and minimal VPC requirements for procurement/infra

I’ll be on the Tue 11/24 11:00 AM PT call (confirmed).
